reviewed_primary_sources.title: Who Trades Bitcoin Futures and Why?
reviewed_primary_sources.authors: Alex Ferko; Amani Moin; Esen Onur; Michael Penick
reviewed_primary_sources.finding: The CFTC-authored study documents changing trader composition, concurrent trader counts and reporting-threshold effects in CME Bitcoin futures, but does not establish that growth or contraction in total reportable trader count predicts subsequent Bitcoin returns.
reviewed_primary_sources.rejection_implication: Trader-count growth can reflect contract maturation, reporting thresholds, micro-contract migration or reactive participation. The source therefore does not select continuation, contrarian or risk-veto direction before outcome access.

reviewed_primary_sources.title: Effects of Index-Fund Investing on Commodity Futures Prices
reviewed_primary_sources.authors: James D. Hamilton; Jing Cynthia Wu
reviewed_primary_sources.finding: The study finds no robust return-predictive evidence from one class of CFTC trader positions and reports that apparent support in another market breaks down out of sample.
reviewed_primary_sources.rejection_implication: CFTC participation measures require an independently specified economic direction and cannot be mined merely because the fields are available.

reviewed_primary_sources.title: CFTC Commitments of Traders Explanatory Notes
reviewed_primary_sources.finding: Official semantics define trader counts as reportable traders by category and side, not unique institutional adoption or capital committed.
reviewed_primary_sources.rejection_implication: A total-trader-count change is not a clean breadth-of-risk-bearing factor without an additional unsupported interpretation.

material_learning: A machine-readable field and a sealed corpus do not create a performance hypothesis. Total reportable trader count has multiple non-predictive structural explanations, and the reviewed primary sources do not select one causal return direction before outcome access.
prohibited_substitutions: Do not inspect trader-count outcomes and then select continuation or contrarian direction.
Do not threshold, smooth, percentile-rank or combine trader counts to rescue the family.
Do not reinterpret total reportable trader count as institutional capital, unique ownership or carry without separate primary evidence.
